description: Are Trickster's serving certificates valid and rotating? Expiry, certificate inventory, hot swaps and watcher errors, and ACME issuance.

panels.title: Soonest expiry
panels.description: Days until the first certificate served by any selected listener and instance expires (negative means already expired). Red under 7 days, orange under 14, yellow under 30. ACME renews in the last third of a certificate's lifetime (about 30 days before a 90-day certificate expires), so an ACME certificate below 30 days means renewal is failing; for files, check the external renewal tool (certbot and cert-manager also renew around 30 days). Short-lived certificate profiles of a few days sit below these thresholds by design. Reads no certificates when no selected listener serves TLS.

panels.title: Expiring < 14 days
panels.description: Number of distinct listener and certificate pairs, on any selected instance, that expire in under 14 days, already-expired ones included. This matches the 14-day warning of the example alerting rules shipped with Trickster.

targets.expr: count(min by (listener, entry) (trickster_tls_certificate_expiration_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener=~"$listener"}) - time() < 14 * 86400) or vector(0)

panels.title: Certs served
panels.description: Distinct listener and certificate pairs in the selected listeners' certificate stores, counting a certificate once however many replicas serve it. Covers every source: backend cert/key files, certificates supplied at runtime (such as Kubernetes TLS Secrets), ACME and config-embedded certificates. An unexpected drop usually means a Secret or backend went away.

targets.expr: count(count by (listener, entry) (trickster_tls_certificate_expiration_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener=~"$listener"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Rejected certs 15m
panels.description: Changed certificate sources, over the last 15 minutes, whose certificate and key failed pair validation and were not swapped in; the last good certificate keeps serving. A bad pair is retried and counted on every watcher poll and file event, so a persistent problem keeps climbing; a single count can be a renewal caught half-written. Red at 3 or more (the example alert fires above 3). Covers watched files and runtime (Kubernetes Secret) certificates, never ACME. All listeners are included.

panels.title: Watcher errors 15m
panels.description: Failed reads of watched certificate, key or CA files over the last 15 minutes (missing file, permissions, unmounted volume). The last good certificate keeps serving, but rotation is stalled until the files are readable. Counted on every poll while the error lasts (about one per tls_watch_interval, default 30s). Red at 3 or more (the example alert fires above 3). All listeners are included.

panels.title: ACME failures
panels.description: Failed ACME order and renewal attempts in the visible time range, all issuers. Each retry of a failing order counts again, so this measures attempts, not certificates: one stuck domain can add many. Expand the ACME row for the issuer and challenge detail. 0 on instances without an acme section.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_acme_orders_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", result="failure"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(trickster_acme_renewals_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", result="failure"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Certificate inventory
panels.description: Every certificate in every selected listener's store, per instance, soonest expiry first. Source is file (backend cert/key files), memory (supplied at runtime, such as Kubernetes TLS Secrets), acme or config. Certificate is the cert file path for files (the same value the validation-failure and watcher-error panels use), otherwise the store entry (memory:<namespace>/<secret>, acme:<issuer>:<domain>, or config: and a content hash that changes on every rotation). Since load resets on every configuration reload even when the file is unchanged, so it shows the last reload or rotation, not the last content change. A certificate that could not be parsed reads as long expired.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_replace(label_replace((min by (instance, listener, entry) (trickster_tls_certificate_expiration_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener=~"$listener"}) - time()) / 86400, "certificate", "$1", "entry", "(.*)"), "certificate", "$1", "entry", "file:([^|]*)[|].*"), "source", "$1", "entry", "([a-z]+):.*")

label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(time() - max by (instance, listener, entry) (trickster_tls_certificate_last_load_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener=~"$listener"}), "certificate", "$1", "entry", "(.*)"), "certificate", "$1", "entry", "file:([^|]*)[|].*"), "source", "$1", "entry", "([a-z]+):.*")

panels.title: Days left, soonest per listener
panels.description: Days until the soonest-expiring certificate of each listener expires, worst instance. A healthy line falls steadily and jumps back up at each renewal; a line that keeps falling through the dashed 30, 14 and 7 day marks means no renewal is reaching the listener. The series are rebuilt on every certificate change, so a single scrape can be missing.

panels.title: Certificate hot swaps by listener
panels.description: Certificates whose content changed while live and were swapped into a listener's store per interval: watched file rotations (tls_watch_interval above 0, default 30s), runtime and Kubernetes Secret updates, and ACME renewals. Established connections keep their old certificate. Not counted: first loads, a rotation that a configuration reload picked up first, config-embedded certificates, and any file rotation when tls_watch_interval is 0. Empty until the first swap.

panels.title: Certificates per listener
panels.description: Entries in each listener's certificate store after its last rebuild, all sources, largest instance. A listener's TLS and HTTP/3 endpoints share one store. With the Kubernetes controller this follows the TLS Secrets that Gateways and Ingresses reference, so a sudden drop points at the controller. The series is rebuilt on each change and can miss one scrape.

panels.title: Validation failures by certificate
panels.description: Certificate sources whose new content failed cert/key pair validation per interval; the last good certificate keeps serving. The legend is the cert file path for watched files (as in the inventory table's Certificate column) or memory:<namespace>/<secret> for runtime certificates. A persistent bad pair is counted on every poll and file event. There is no listener label, so the Listener filter does not apply. Empty until the first failure.

panels.title: Watcher read errors by certificate
panels.description: Failed reads of a watched cert, key or CA file per interval, by the set's cert file path (as in the inventory table's Certificate column). A steady stream at about one per tls_watch_interval means the files are gone or unreadable and rotation is stalled; the last good certificate keeps serving. There is no listener label, so the Listener filter does not apply. Empty until the first error.

panels.title: Certs obtained
panels.description: New (non-renewal) certificates this fleet obtained from its ACME issuers in the visible time range, one per domain. Certificates loaded from ACME storage at startup are not counted, and with shared Redis or Valkey storage only the replica that performed the issuance counts it. Needs a top-level acme section; 0 otherwise.

panels.title: Order failures
panels.description: Failed attempts to obtain a new certificate in the visible time range. Every retry inside the ACME client's backoff loop counts, so this can far exceed the number of domains and cannot be divided by the obtained count into a success rate. The application log has the CA's error.

panels.title: Renewals
panels.description: Successful certificate renewals in the visible time range, one per domain. Renewal starts in the last third of a certificate's lifetime (or when the CA's renewal information says so), so this is often 0 over short ranges; widen the time range or rely on Soonest expiry. Each renewal also appears as a hot swap on every listener serving the name.

panels.title: Renewal failures
panels.description: Failed renewal attempts in the visible time range, counted per retry like order failures, so read it as a signal, not a rate. The current certificate keeps serving until it expires; watch Soonest expiry.

panels.title: Startup wait
panels.description: Longest time, across the selected instances, that the current process held readiness at startup waiting for missing ACME certificates (acme.wait_on_startup above 0). 0 when no wait was configured, every certificate was already in storage, or the instance has no ACME. Equals wait_on_startup when the wait timed out. Set once per process; reloads do not change it.

panels.title: Startup timeouts
panels.description: Instances whose current process released readiness at startup before every managed name had a certificate (wait_on_startup elapsed). Those names failed handshakes until issued, and issuance kept retrying in the background. Resets when the process restarts.

panels.title: ACME orders and renewals by issuer
panels.description: ACME issuance events per interval by issuer: new-certificate orders and renewals, success or failure. A success is one certificate for one domain; a failure is one attempt, and the ACME client retries with backoff, so a failing domain shows as repeated failure bars until it succeeds. Empty until the first event.

panels.title: ACME challenge requests/s
panels.description: Validation traffic by challenge type and result. http-01: requests under /.well-known/acme-challenge/ on a plaintext port; served matched a pending challenge, unknown got an empty 404. tls-alpn-01: handshakes offering only the acme-tls/1 protocol; served returned a validation certificate, error means ACME had none for that name, unknown means no ACME solver is registered. unknown is mostly scanner noise and can appear on TLS listeners without ACME. CAs validate from several vantage points, so one challenge gives several served.

panels.title: On-demand issuance decisions/s
panels.description: Decisions for TLS handshakes naming a host no stored certificate covers, on listeners with acme.on_demand. allowed: issuance may start (see orders for the outcome). refused: not in allowed_domains, or the ask endpoint said no. refused_cached: a refusal remembered for decision_ttl. rate_limited: over on_demand.rate_limit issuances per minute. ask_error: the ask endpoint failed. A burst of refusals is usually clients probing random names.
